form.title: Product information template: Regulatory enrolment process (REP)
errorSummary.form.name: The form
warning.text:
This template is used to file submissions (regulatory activities) with Health Canada.


The web-based Extensible Markup Language (XML) product information (REP PI XML) file is required only for a subset of regulatory activities submitted through the electronic submissions gateway (ESG). Refer to “Product information (PI) template and process” section of the guidance document Regulatory enrolment process (REP): Drugs for human/veterinary use, disinfectants, and biocides.


Ensure that all fields in this template are completed in the sequential order. The selections made in certain fields may affect the visibility and availability of other fields and sections throughout the form.
ht.load.file.1: A file should not be loaded if this is the first time enrolling the company.
amend.alert: The "Amend enrolment" button must be selected when amending a final company XML.

pediatric.pilot.question.text1:
If filing an NDS or an SNDS that includes a change listed below, please submit thepediatric pilot survey with your filing:

  • new indication
  • new dosage form
  • new route of administration
clinical.trial: Does this submission include clinical trial data?
clinical.sex: Are the clinical trial data in your submission disaggregated by sex (male or female) by?
clinical.age: Are the clinical trial data in your submission disaggregated by age by?
clinical.race: Are the clinical trial data in your submission disaggregated by race / ethnicity by?
clinical.pedi: Does this submission include clinical trial data from pediatric populations (those under 18 years of age)?
isSchedule: in schedule C (radiopharmaceuticals) to the Food and Drugs Act
isInclude: included in schedule D (biologics) to the Food and Drugs Act
isRegulated: regulated under the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act
isNonPrescriptioScheduleApplied: a non-prescription drug to which one or more schedule A claims apply
isDrugPermitted: a drug permitted to be sold without a prescription but administered only under the supervision of a practitioner
ht.load.file.2: When continuing with a working copy, the format of the file to load should be .hcsc.
ht.load.file.3: When viewing/updating a final XML file, the format of the file to load should be .xml.
ht.product.info.2: Please only include information that is pertinent to this regulatory activity (i.e. if the dossier has 5 dosage forms, but this regulatory activity only applies to 1, only list the formulation for that 1 dosage form in this version of the product information XML file).
ht.product.info.3: The company identifier must be obtained from the final company XML file, issued by Health Canada.
ht.product.info.4: The dossier identifier can be obtained from Health Canada issued document. The format of a dossier identifier is a letter followed by six digits. (e.g. x######).
ht.product.info.5: Note: Each section with a Save record button must be saved individually; otherwise incomplete information will be lost.
ht.company.id.2: The Company identifier can be obtained from the latest Health Canada issued final company XML file, or the 'company code' found on the Annual Drug Notification Form (ADNF).
ht.company.id.3: Company identifier must be 5 digits, add leading zero when required.
ht.dossier.type.2: Biologic dossier applies to all biologic products and radiopharmaceuticals.
ht.dossier.type.3: Pharmaceutical dossier applies to all pharmaceutical products, non-prescription and ethical products, and disinfectants.
ht.dossier.type.4: Veterinary dossier applies to all pharmaceuticals for veterinary use, non-prescription and ethical products.
ht.product.name.2: Only include the name of the products impacted by this regulatory activity. For multiple products, list and separate their product names with a semi-colon (;).
ht.product.name.3: The product name is the name assigned by the manufacturer /sponsor to distinguish the drug (product) and under which the drug is to be sold/advertised. It is also the name used to identify the product in all correspondence related to the submission and on the product label(s) and Product Monograph and/or Package Insert, if applicable. If the brand name has not yet been determined, the proper or common name of the drug or the research code may be used.
ht.product.name.4: The product name input in this field will only be reviewed with the initial transaction of a dossier (i.e. sequence 0000 for eCTD format). For all subsequent transactions, any changes to the product name should be captured and will be reviewed using the regulatory transaction template. Product name changes on this template will not be reviewed.
ht.proper.name.2: The proper name for a product is the name assigned to the drug in Section C.01.002 of the Food and Drug Regulations, or in boldface type in other Sections of the Regulations or the name of the drug in its finished form identified in the title of a monograph or in any of the official publications listed in Schedule B to the Food and Drugs Act. Example: Acetaminophen, Ferrous Sulphate Tablets.
ht.proper.name.3: The common name is the name by which a single ingredient drug is commonly known / designated in scientific or technical journals other than the publications referred to in Schedule B to the Food and Drugs Act. The common name includes the pharmaceutical form when used in relation to the finished drug product.
ht.proper.name.4: If there is no proper name and the drug is comprised of a single medicinal ingredient, enter the common name.
ht.proper.name.5: If there is no proper name and the drug is comprised of more than one medicinal ingredient, the proper name of the ingredients should be captured and separated by a forward slash (/).
ht.proper.name.6: If there are multiple finished products, list all proper, common or non-proprietary names included in the field 4. Product Name and separate them with a coma (,).
ht.is.admin.submission.3: Guidance Administrative Processing of Submissions and Applications Involving Human or Disinfectant Drugs.
ht.is.admin.submission.4: For instructions regarding administrative submission for veterinary drugs, please contact
ht.address.to.send.2: If DNF/NOC are to be sent to the manufacturer /sponsor, please ensure the information in your final company XML file is up to date.
ht.address.to.send.3: In addition for importers, please ensure the applicable importers are identified in section 7 below.
ht.address.to.send.4: If DNF/NOC are to be sent to the contact for this regulatory activity, the contact listed on the latest Regulatory Transaction XML file for this regulatory activity will used.
ht.importer.2: When the manufacturer /sponsor is not located in Canada, a Canadian Importer must be identified.
ht.importer.3: Only list the importers associated with Drug identification numbers (DINs) identified in the formulation section below.
ht.route.id.2: The routing identifier is a unique identifier within the Common Electronic Submissions Gateway (CESG) used to identify specific gateway account, whether it uses the Applicability Statement 2 (AS2) or WebTrader interfaces.
ht.route.id.3: For the WebTrader users, the routing identifier is automatically assigned to each account by the system. It can be retrieved from the receipt message. Navigate to the WebTrader Inbox, click on “Receipt”, “View” document. Document Content page opens up and the routing identifier can be found under attribute: “X-Cyclone-To:”
ht.route.id.4: For the AS2 users, the routing identifier has to be created by the company. It is recommended that the company's data universal numbering system number be used, but any alpha-numeric text string is acceptable.
ht.route.id.5: The routing identifier could be the same for the manufacturer / sponsor contact and regulatory / annual contact. The Canadian importer would have a separate routing identifier.
ht.route.id.6: For any further questions on the routing identifier, please contact the Food and Drug Administration Help Desk at
ht.drug.use.2: Indicate whether the drug is intended for human use, veterinary use, as a radiopharmaceutical, as a disinfectant, or as a drug and medical device.
ht.din.2: If there are multiple Drug identification numbers, separate them with a coma (,).
ht.use.dosage.2: Indicate the proposed indication/use of the drug, e.g. for use in the treatment of angina and hypertension, to treat the symptoms of hay fever, for the prophylaxis of measles virus infection.
ht.use.dosage.3: For a new drug, the proposed indication/use shall be a summary of the indication described in the product monograph. Key scientific terminology should be used for this section.
ht.use.dosage.4: Referring to the product monograph will only be accepted if there's no change to the indication.
ht.use.dosage.5: For Disinfectants, proposed indications as "disinfectant /sanitizer" or "toilet bowl cleaner" are not permitted.
ht.use.dosage.6: Indicate the proposed dosage - (by age – include maximum daily dose).
ht.formulation.2: If the submission /application contains different formulations (e.g., multiple strengths), please add the product name (if unique) or the strength for proper identification.
ht.formulation.3: For consumer health products, if there are multiple products, please include each as a stand alone formulation in the same order if the product names listed in field 4. Product Name.
ht.formulation.4: For diluents, adjuvants and placebos, either include them as non-medicinal ingredients in the same formulation and use “diluent”, “adjuvant”, “placebo” as the variant for identification purposes or provide them as a stand alone formulation.
ht.formulation.5: The formulation identifier is auto generated by the template when you click on “Add formulation”.
ht.formulation.6: Copy button: After saving ingredient / formulation details, you may choose to copy those details into a new ingredient / formulation record and change one or more fields as required. This will help minimize the amount of data entry for similar ingredients / formulations.
ht.formulation.7: For each ingredient/material identified as animal or human sourced, you must provide additional details by completing section 13 of this template.
ht.form.num.2: The formulation identifier is auto generated by the template when you click on “Add Formulations”.
ht.form.num.3: Copy button: After saving ingredient / formulation details, sponsors may choose to copy those details into a new ingredient / formulation record and change one or more fields as required. This will help minimize the amount of data entry for similar ingredients / formulations.
ht.ingredients.2: A “Copy record” button is available for duplicating the ingredient section. This is useful for non-medicinal ingredient that is present in different quantities in various variants. Be sure to update the appropriate fields (e.g. variant name, ingredient strength) and verify that the information in the remaining fields is accurate.
ht.ingredients.3: Note: This feature is only available after creating the ingredient entry and expanding that entry. The “Copy record” button is at the bottom of that section next to “Delete Record” button.
ht.ingredients.4: For additional details like overages and adjustments, select “other” in the unit field for a free text field.
ht.ingredients.5: For ingredients present in "quantum satis", the following should be selected: Operator: "equal", Value: "1", and Units: "q.s."
ht.ingredients.6: For ingredients used in adjusting pH, the following should be selected: Operator: "equal", Value: "1", Units: "other", and Other unit details: "adjust pH"
ht.prop.unknown.2: If uncertain whether the proprietary information reference source is acceptable, please contact the appropriate review bureau in advance of filing.
ht.prop.unknown.3: For more information regarding administrative cross-licensing agreements please refer to the Guidance Document:
ht.prop.unknown.4: Administrative Processing of Submissions and Applications Involving Human or Disinfectant Drugs.
ht.prop.known.4: Cross licensing Agreement Control number XXXXXXX
ht.prop.known.5: The control number of the submission or application most recently approved for the licensor drug. Please note that the word “approved” would function to exclude NCs, which are not approved but rather issued No Objection Letters.
ht.prop.known.6: For more information regarding administrative cross-licensing agreements please refer to the Guidance Document:
ht.prop.known.7: Administrative Processing of Submissions and Applications Involving Human or Disinfectant Drugs.
ht.ingredient.name.2: Sponsors should always select the medicinal ingredient name from the searchable list where possible. If the medicinal ingredient name is not found in the list, enter the new medicinal ingredient name in this field using the International Non Proprietary (INN) terminology, as it is the Health Canada’s standard to assign the preferred name to ingredients. If there is no existing INN terminology for the ingredient, you are required to use other recognized standards terminology in the following order: United States Adopted Names, Martindale, Merck Index, Hawley’s Condensed Chemical Dictionary, the Handbook of Pharmaceutical Excipient, International Cosmetics Ingredient Dictionary and Handbook, information available online.
ht.form.variant.2: For formulation variations pertaining to the same DIN (for example [e.g.] multiple flavourings, colours, fragrances), identify the variant name associated with each non-medicinal ingredient (NMI). Example:
ht.form.variant.3: If a NMI is the same quantity in all variants, then it only needs to be listed once and the variant name field should indicate “All variants”.
ht.form.variant.4: If a NMI pertains to only one variant, then the variant name should be entered (e.g., apple flavour).
ht.form.variant.5: If the NMI is in various variants, at different quantities, the variant name field should be entered each time.
ht.purpose.2: Examples: preservative, colouring agent or capsule shell, etc.
ht.standard.2: Where the standard of manufacture of an ingredient complies with a Schedule B compendial standard, use the applicable abbreviation for that compendium, e.g. United States Pharmacopeia (USP), British Pharmacopoeia (BP). Where the specifications for ingredient manufacture deviate from and exceed, or are equivalent to the compendial standard, manufacturer's standard (Mfr Std) may be indicated. Please enter N/A if no compendial standard exists for the active ingredient.
ht.nano.2: Select the appropriate option based on Health Canada's working definition of Nanomaterials:
ht.nano.3: Health Canada considers any manufactured product, material, substance, ingredient, device, system or structure to be nanomaterial if:
ht.nano.3.1: It is at or within the nanoscale in at least one spatial dimension, or;
ht.nano.3.2: It is smaller or larger than the nanoscale in all spatial dimensions and exhibits one or more nanoscale phenomena.
ht.nano.4: For the purposes of this definition:
ht.nano.4.1: The term “nanoscale” means 1 to 100 nanometres, inclusive;
ht.nano.4.2: The term “nanoscale phenomena” means properties of the product, material, substance, ingredient, device, system or structure which are attributable to its size and distinguishable from the chemical or physical properties of individual atoms, individual molecules and bulk material; and,
ht.nano.4.3: The term “manufactured” includes engineering processes and control of matter and processes at the nanoscale.
ht.bio.source.2: Select yes if this ingredient/material was human or animal sourced at any stage in the manufacture of the drug product including excipient or processing aid source from human and/or animal tissue.
ht.bio.source.3: If “Yes” is selected, please ensure you are required to complete section 13 of this template.
ht.bio.used.2: If “Yes” is selected, please ensure you are required to complete section 13 of this template.
ht.bio.used.3: Enter chemical abstracts service (CAS) (if applicable), material name and standard for the human/animal sourced material (other than the ingredient listed in the formulation above) used in the manufacturing of the product.
ht.bio.used.4: Select the option “Yes” for the question “Present in final container” if the ingredient is present in the final container (based on the quality standard applicable for the product).
ht.pack.size.2: Multiple pack sizes per container type can be displayed as:
ht.shelf.life.2: The proposed expiry/shelf life is the length of time in years and months up to which the drug product maintains its labelled potency, purity and physical characteristics.
ht.countries.2: Provide the name of the country(ies) where the final dosage form of the drug product is manufactured /fabricated, e.g., if the drug product is in the dosage form of a tablet or solution, enter the country(ies) where the tablet or solution was fabricated. This may not necessarily be the country(ies) where the product is packaged/labeled.
ht.bio.source.ingre.2: List the animal/human-sourced material(s) for each individual drug product ingredient and/or material used at any stage in the manufacture of the drug product including excipient or processing aid source from human and/or animal tissue.
ht.bio.source.ingre.3: The “Ingredient or material name” field in this section is case-sensitive and must match exactly with the ingredient/material name listed in the formulation tab. If it does not match, the following errors may be displayed:“There are errors with the human or animal sourced records, missing source” or “There are errors with the human or animal sourced records, extra source”.
ht.generate.final.2: A final product information XML file can be included in:
ht.generate.final.2.1: For Human Drugs - section 1.2.1 of your transaction using REP.
ht.generate.final.2.2: For Veterinary Drugs - section 1.5 of your transaction using REP
ht.generate.final.3: Refer to the REP guidance document for detailed information on when it is required.
ht.data.ques.2: If you have any questions about how to answer this questionnaire, please contact the Centre for Policy, Pediatrics and International Collaboration by email at
ht.clinical.trial.2: This question is asking if clinical trials were used to gather evidence for the therapeutic product.
ht.clinical.sex.2: This question is asking if all or part of your clinical evidence can be / has been analysed by male participants versus female participants.
ht.clinical.sex.3: This question is asking whether efficacy data has been disaggregated by male vs. female. Note: this question is not asking if statistically significant findings are available for efficacy when analysed by sex.
ht.clinical.sex.4: This question is asking whether safety data has been disaggregated by male vs. female. Note: this question is not asking if statistically significant findings are available for safety when analysed by sex.
ht.clinical.age.2: This question is asking if all or part of your clinical evidence can be analysed by distinct age categories. For example, can the results of 18-64 year olds be compared to 65+ year olds? If children are included in the trials, can evidence be analysed by specific, clinically relevant pediatric age ranges (if relevant)?
ht.clinical.age.3: This question is asking whether efficacy data can be disaggregated by distinct age categories. Note: this question is not asking if statistically significant findings are available for efficacy when analysed by age.
ht.clinical.age.4: This question is asking whether safety data can be disaggregated by distinct age categories. Note: this question is not asking if statistically significant findings are available for safety when analysed by age.
ht.clinical.race.2: This question is asking if all or part of your clinical evidence can be analysed by distinct racial and/or ethnic groups. For example, can the evidence be analysed for Black, Asian or Hispanic clinical trial participants?
ht.clinical.race.3: This question is asking whether efficacy data can be disaggregated by racial and/or ethnic subpopulations. Note: this question is not asking if statistically significant findings are available for efficacy when analysed by race/ethnicity.
ht.clinical.race.4: This question is asking whether safety data can be disaggregated by racial and/or ethnic subpopulations. Note: this question is not asking if statistically significant findings are available for safety when analysed by race/ethnicity.
ht.clinical.pedi.2: This question is asking if pediatric populations (i.e. under the age of 18) were included in any of the clinical trial data you are submitting.
schedule.claim.applied: Select the diseases and disorders that apply to the claims made (select at least one)
schedule.claim.applied.detail.title: Schedule A claim details
schedule.claim.applied.detail: Provide information below for non prescription products that have associated schedule A claims only.
schedule.a.claim.and.indication: Please list the schedule A claims and indications associated with this product
disinfectant.type.title: Disinfectant type (please select at least one disinfectant type)
